A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ladder Residual research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including identifying substantive removals.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference benchmarks, training and adaptation results, Desynced Residual experiments, and profiler traces.

after.justification: v5 reports original inference benchmarks, training and adaptation results, larger-model comparisons, and profiler traces.

M1.justification: v5 removes Desynced Residual, the separate architecture that selectively drops AllReduce operations, including its 2x and 4x variants. This removes a substantial proposed method. Ladder Residual's recurrence and asynchronous execution procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The FineWeb-edu and Infinity-Instruct training coverage, downstream benchmark suite, and inference scenarios remain. Larger model configurations do not introduce new tasks. The NVLink-to-P2P terminology revision describes the existing communication control rather than establishing a newly tested environment.

E2.justification: The principal standard Transformer, parallel attention/MLP, communication-free upper-bound, and original Llama comparisons remain. However, v1 Table 6's secondary comparison of Ladder against Desynced Residual-2x and -4x disappears. The new larger-Ladder comparison reuses the standard Transformer baseline.

E3.justification: v5 adds unequal-size comparisons: 1.5B Ladder versus 1.2B standard, and 4.5B Ladder versus 3.5B standard, trained on 100B tokens. Existing pretraining sizes are reported as 1.2B/3.5B instead of 1B/3B, with unchanged Table 3 scores; this does not establish rerunning. Retained training budgets, evaluation metrics, and the P2P-disabling command remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The Desynced Residual investigation of communication frequency, attention versus MLP synchronization, and quality–latency tradeoffs is removed. v5 Section 5.2 instead adds an analysis of whether larger Ladder models can improve quality while retaining higher throughput. The adaptation-depth comparison, Pareto analysis, and appendix profiler evidence remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Updated point estimates and additional result rows do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises the retrained 16-layer model under unchanged stated adaptation settings: average 56.24 to 57.61, GSM8K 80.29 to 86.81, and TruthfulQA 39.66 to 37.58. v5 Table 5 adds larger-Ladder quality and throughput results, while v1's Desynced Residual Tables 5–6 disappear. Hybrid inference speedup becomes 21%, replacing v1's inconsistent 14.5% in Section 4.2 and 23% in the conclusion.

T1.justification: The tensor-parallel algebra and standard/Ladder recurrences in Equations 1–2 are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs. Removing the procedural Desynced Residual proposal does not remove a separate theoretical result.

C1.justification: v1 presents both communication overlapping and communication dropping as contributions, including eliminating 75% of communication with little quality loss. v5 removes the Desynced Residual contribution from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, narrowing the paper to Ladder Residual. Its introduction also drops the qualification about slightly worse coding performance.

C2.justification: v5 reframes P2P-disabled measurements as simulating slow communication rather than directly representing absent NVLink. It adds pipeline-boundary compatibility explanations and interprets larger-model results as a quality–throughput tradeoff. The discussion of Desynced Residual's usefulness when communication cannot be fully overlapped is removed.

D1.justification: v5 adds pipeline tensor-transfer/API details and an Open LM Engine pretraining pointer. It removes v1's dedicated inference-code link, replaces the training-code reference, and omits the NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1 disclosure. These are documentation and access-information changes; the PDFs do not establish that code became unavailable.

R1.justification: The Graham et al. (2016) SHARP citation and reference are removed with the SHARP discussion. The related-work section otherwise retains substantially the same cited works and positioning of architectural changes against kernel-level communication optimizations.

P1.justification: v5 tightens the abstract, introduction, and benchmarking prose, consolidates the background headings, replaces the Desynced Residual section with Discussion, and adds an Impact Statement. Most retained technical exposition and the overall section sequence remain close to v1.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column conference layout. Figure 2 merges eight panels into four, Figure 3 is redrawn, Desynced Residual displays disappear, and a larger-model Table 5 is added. The unchanged profiler image becomes Figure 5. Figure 2 introduces misleading batch-size axis labels where tensor-parallel size varies.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful evidence about the quality–throughput tradeoff in Table 5, clarifies the P2P experiment, and makes hybrid-speed statements consistent. However, it removes the substantive Desynced Residual study and dedicated inference-code pointer, and introduces incorrect Figure 2 axis labels. The narrower focus and added analysis have benefits, but their net value against lost evidence, reduced reproducibility information, and the display error is unclear.
